hook: The general who conquered Gaul, crossed the Rubicon, and was stabbed on the Ides of March.

pages.x: As a young man, Caesar was seized by pirates, who asked a ransom of 20 talents of silver. He laughed and told them he was worth at least 50. For 38 days he joked with them, read them his poems and promised to crucify them. Once freed, he raised a fleet, caught them, and did.

Caesar came from an old but poor noble family. He borrowed huge sums to put on games and win votes, and became Rome's chief priest in 63 BC. In 60 BC he made a pact with Pompey and Crassus, and the next year became consul, the top job in the Republic.

From 58 to 50 BC he conquered Gaul, roughly modern France and Belgium, and crossed into Britain and Germany. At Alesia in 52 BC he trapped the Gallic leader Vercingetorix inside a ring of walls, while building a second ring outside to hold off a relief army. He told the story himself in his Commentaries.

In January 49 BC the Senate ordered him to give up his army. Leading soldiers across the Rubicon, the stream that marked Italy's border, was against the law. He crossed with one legion, saying: "The die is cast." "Crossing the Rubicon" still means passing the point of no return.

pages.t: I came, I saw, I conquered
pages.x: He beat Pompey and his allies from Spain to Egypt, and reported one quick victory in Turkey in three words: "Veni, vidi, vici." As dictator he gave land to his veterans and brought in a new calendar of 365 days with a leap year, the basis of the one we use. July is named after him.

Fearing he would make himself king, about 60 senators led by Brutus and Cassius stabbed him 23 times at a meeting of the Senate on 15 March 44 BC. He fell at the foot of a statue of Pompey. Shakespeare gave him the words "Et tu, Brute?" when he saw his friend Brutus among the killers.

Caesar's murder did not save the Republic: his adopted son Augustus became the first emperor. His name became a title for rulers, Kaiser in German and tsar in Russian, and his calendar is still in use.
pts: Won a civil war and became dictator of Rome
Gave us the 365-day calendar and the month of July
His name became the word for emperor
